item.title: After Michigan Loss, AIPAC Weighs a Second Effort to Defeat El-Sayed
item.description: The pro-Israel organization spent $32 million in an unsuccessful effort to defeat Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary. It might try again in the general election.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Medina and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: AIPAC’s super PAC spent $32 million to boost the opponent of Dr. Abdul El-Sayed in the primary.

item.title: El-Sayed’s Michigan Senate Primary Win Sets Up the Left’s Biggest Test of the Fall
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed’s Senate candidacy poses a critical challenge for Democrats’ ascendant progressive wing: Can an insurgent candidate, with unabashedly liberal positions, win a general election in a moderate state?
item.dc:creator: Lisa Lerer
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed greeting the audience at his election watch party in Detroit.

item.title: Mayor Says El-Sayed’s Win Shows He Is More Than a ‘Mini-Mamdani’
item.description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York said that Dr. Abdul El-Sayed’s close victory in the Michigan Senate primary put “working-class Americans back at the heart of our politics.”
item.dc:creator: Jeffery C. Mays
item.media:credit: Vincent Alban for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mayor Zohran Mamdani of New York last month at Gracie Mansion in Manhattan. Mr. Mamdani was asked on Wednesday about similarities between him and Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, who won Michigan’s Democratic Senate primary.

item.title: Michigan Democrats Pick El-Sayed
item.description: Also, the Senate confirms a new C.D.C. director. Here’s the latest at the end of Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Cullen
item.media:credit: Nick Hagen for The New York Times
item.media:description: Abdul El-Sayed at his election watch party in Detroit last night.

item.title: Suspected Iran Cyberattacks on U.S. Water Supply Follow Years of Warnings and Neglect
item.description: Federal and state officials are racing to address an assault on the nation’s water supply that they believe is the work of Iranian hackers.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Nicole Craine for The New York Times
item.media:description: A water treatment plant in Georgia earlier this year. Officials have long warned that the nation’s roughly 150,000 water treatment systems are relatively easy targets for hackers.

item.title: Helicopter Carrying Trump Flies Near Passenger Jet in Washington Airspace
item.description: Marine One, the helicopter that ferries the president, came within less than a mile of an Envoy Air flight on Tuesday, raising new concerns about air traffic control in the congested area.
item.dc:creator: Kate Kelly
item.media:credit: Doug Mills/The New York Times
item.media:description: Marine One, right, carrying President Trump, flying to Joint Base Andrews on Tuesday.

item.title: Trump Said Qatari Jet Was Destined for His Library. That May Change.
item.description: A White House official says no final decision has been made about which plane will go on display at the Trump presidential library. That leaves the fate of the Qatari jet unclear.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman and Eric Lipton
item.category: Trump, Donald J, Presidential Library and Museum
item.media:credit: Allison Robbert for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Donald J. Trump unveiling the Qatari-donated 747-8 as the new VC-25B Bridge plane at Joint Base Andrews in June.

item.title: C.I.A. Sets Up Secret Cuba Task Force as Trump Pressures Havana
item.description: The task force will allow the spy agency to quickly direct more financial, human and technical resources at the island, with the goal of creating fissures among the Cuban political elite.
item.dc:creator: Adam Entous
item.media:credit: Todd Heisler/The New York Times
item.media:description: Havana in 2019. The C.I.A.’s action coincides with stepped-up efforts by U.S. intelligence agencies to get a better understanding of the situation on the ground inside Cuba.

item.title: Why Congress Wants a Closer U.S.-Israel Defense Partnership
item.description: A proposal making its way through Congress would integrate the U.S. and Israeli defense and intelligence apparatuses more tightly. Some worry that it is a bad idea.
item.dc:creator: Robert Jimison
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross/The New York Times
item.media:description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of Israel has engaged in a public campaign to appear less reliant on U.S. military aid as President Trump urges allies to contribute more meaningfully to their own defense.

item.title: Iran Says It Is Nearing Final Agreement With Oman on Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The agreement on an acceptable route for ships to pass through the strait would effectively ratify Tehran’s control over the crucial waterway.

item.title: Star Scholar Jason Arday Resigns From Cambridge
item.description: Jason Arday was hired by the University of Cambridge in 2023 as the youngest Black professor in its history. Doubt has since been cast on his academic qualifications and claims about his life.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor and Jennifer Schuessler

item.title: Cambridge Professor Jason Arday’s Work Challenged Ahead of Book Launch
item.description: A knife-wielding masked man. A pig’s head outside his parents’ door. Running 30 marathons in 35 days. The Cambridge professor Jason Arday, accused of plagiarism, says he’s been through it all. Not everyone believes him.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Schuessler and Alexandra Alter
item.media:credit: via Simon & Schuster; Photo by Anselm Ebulue

item.title: U.S. Cuts Ties With Organ Donor Group After Reports of Abuses
item.description: The federal government is ending its contract with a Kentucky nonprofit that it says pressured medical workers to remove organs from patients who were getting better.
item.dc:creator: Brian M. Rosenthal
item.media:credit: Luke Sharrett for The New York Times
item.media:description: The offices of Network for Hope, an organ donation organization, in Louisville, Ky.

item.title: Lobga Rangzen, the Tibetan Activist Who Set Himself on Fire in Manhattan
item.description: No one doubted the intensity of Lobga Rangzen’s commitment to a Tibet free of Chinese control. But they were not prepared for what he did next.
item.dc:creator: Vivian Wang and Vincent Alban
item.media:description: A shrine for Lobga Rangzen, a Tibetan activist who self immolated in protest for Tibet’s independence from China, outside the United Nations building in July.

item.title: Death Renews Scrutiny of Delaney Hall. Here’s What to Know.

item.dc:creator: Ana Ley
item.media:credit: Lexi Parra/The New York Times
item.media:description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents have monitored demonstrations outside the Delaney Hall detention center for months.

item.title: ICE Threatens Sheriffs In Chicago and Minneapolis With Prosecution Over Access to Inmates
item.description: In a new tactic, federal immigration officials recently started saying they would criminally charge the elected county sheriffs in Minneapolis and Chicago.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Londoño and Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:credit: Charles Rex Arbogast/Associated Press, Jamie Kelter Davis for The New York Times
item.media:description: Tom Dart, the sheriff of Cook County, Ill., left, and Dawanna S. Witt, sheriff of Hennepin County, Minn., have both been given warnings, conveyed in a series of letters that federal agents began hand-delivering in early July.
